learned: Law is about understanding the rules that organize society and applying them carefully to real situations. You read closely, reason step by step, argue your position, and write clearly.

ladder.note: You research, prepare documents, and support a lawyer on real cases. In many countries you also need extra exams or training to practise as a lawyer.

ladder.roles: Associate lawyer, in-house counsel, prosecutor, legal advisor
ladder.note: You handle your own cases or clients and specialize in an area such as contracts or business law.

ladder.roles: Partner, senior counsel, head of legal, judge
ladder.note: You lead cases or teams, advise on high-stakes decisions, and shape how an organization handles legal risk.

outlook: Law graduates can work in many places, not only in courtrooms. The route to becoming a practising lawyer differs from country to country, so check the requirements in the place where you plan to work.
